Il pneumotorace si riconosce dalla linea: A pneumothorax is recognised by the visceral pleural line: a thin white line parallel to the chest wall, beyond which there are no lung markings. When standing the air rises to the apex; when supine it goes anterior and inferior (deep sulcus sign). Skin folds and the scapular borders can mimic it: the pleural line is thin and curved, a fold is thicker and often continues beyond the thorax. On follow-up after drainage check three things: how much air remains, where the tube runs (side holes inside the thorax) and whether subcutaneous emphysema appears. Mediastinal shift to the healthy side with a flattened diaphragm indicates a tension pneumothorax, which is a clinical emergency. Comparison with the previous exam is the core of these follow-ups: same projection, same window, look first at the problem area (here the left apex) and then at everything else. After drain removal the X-ray is used to exclude recurrence of the pneumothorax and complications at the insertion site (subcutaneous emphysema, effusion).
